message.content:
**Masses (atomic‑mass units)**  

| Particle | Mass (amu) |
|----------|------------|
| **Proton** | **≈ 1.007 276 467 amu** |
| **Neutron** | **≈ 1.008 664 916 amu** |

These values come directly from the latest CODATA recommendations (proton mass \(m_{\rm p}=938.272\,0813\;\text{MeV}/c^{2}\), neutron mass \(m_{\rm n}=939.565\,4133\;\text{MeV}/c^{2}\)).  
They differ only slightly from “one nucleon” (\(\approx 1.009\) amu) because of nuclear binding energies.

---

### Spatial Extent – Diameters

Because both particles are composite objects made of quarks bound by gluons, they do not have sharp surfaces like macroscopic spheres. Experimental determinations usually quote a *root‑mean‑square* (RMS) radius derived from scattering experiments. A convenient way to express this is as a “diameter”, i.e., twice the RMS radius.

| Particle | RMS Radius (fm) | Approximate Diameter (fm) |
|----------|-----------------|---------------------------|
| **Proton** | \(\displaystyle r_{E,p}=0.842\pm0.004~{\rm fm}\) *(charge radius)* | \(\displaystyle d_{p}\simeq 1.684~{\rm fm}\) |
| **Neutron** | \(\displaystyle r_{\!n}^{\rm eff}\!\approx0.85–0.90~{\rm fm}\) *(effective matter radius)* | \(\displaystyle d_{n}\simeq 1.70–1.80~{\rm fm}\) |

#### Notes & Sources

1. **Proton:**  
   • Charge‐radius measurements from electron–scattering and muonic hydrogen spectroscopy converge at roughly \(0.842\) fm (CODATA 2018).  
   • Doubling gives a diameter of about \(1.68\) fm.

2. **Neutron:**  
   • No net charge means there isn’t a single “electromagnetic” radius. Instead, analyses of elastic scattering and form factors yield an effective matter radius close to that of the proton—typically quoted between \(0.85\) and \(0.90\) fm.  
   • Thus the diameter lies near \(1.7\)–\(1.8\) fm.

If you require even finer precision (for instance, including higher‑order QED corrections or lattice‑QCD results), let me know—I can pull up the most recent numerical tables.
